content: Hi, do you want your own #rss-like stream of commits to the FLT repo inside this channel, like #CSLib > Recent commits to cslib or #PhysLean > Recent commits to PhysLean?
Not me personally, because I'm basically the only person merging the PRs, but if others do then I won't object.

AI is merging bump commits now so all of a sudden I am much keener on this. In fact I thought we set it up already and I merged the bumps to the new version of lean so I was expecting a message saying that FLT had just got quicker, but I don't remember seeing one. Am I just confused?
There's #rss > Significant commits to FLT but not a "recent commits" RSS

Thanks! I don't need a "recent commits", significant commits is fine (thanks for pointing this out, I was searching for the wrong thing, sorry for the ping Joscha). So my revised question is "how come when everyone else bumped to v4.34.0-rc1 they got a speedup in their significant commits, but I didn't? Is it still working?"

More precisely, given what happened to lots of other repos, I was expecting https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/pull/1161 to have a nontrivial effect on compile time. Does it not? If not, then it would perhaps be interesting to know what distinguishes FLT from other repos (see for example the mathlib commit #rss > Significant commits to mathlib4 @ 💬 and the Tau Ceti commit #Tau Ceti > radar reports @ 💬 )
Oh, !radar seems to work on FLT so I can answer this myself

You can also look at https://radar.lean-lang.org/repos/flt to see the radar results for any already merged commits. That PR does show improved performance, it was just below whatever calculation is done for the significance threshold.
Yeah, apparently a global speed-up of 1.6% is enough to get mathlib and TauCeti excited, but not FLT :shrug:

Woah, roughly the same percentage diff across all projects seems wild, is that common?
#rss > Significant commits to mathlib4 @ 💬
#Tau Ceti > radar reports @ 💬
All I know is that I was worried it was -1.6% on mathlib and -0% on FLT, so at least that's something off my mind! That was what prompted this thread in the first place.
